lines: 2-week history of facial rash and joint pain affecting hands and wrists with increased sensitivity to sunlight
A 28-year-old woman presents with a 2-week history of facial rash and joint pain affecting her hands and wrists.
She reports morning stiffness lasting about an hour and increased sensitivity to sunlight.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO three times daily
Her temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Physical examination findings are shown below.
Laboratory tests reveal positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA), positive anti–double-stranded DNA antibodies, and low complement C3 and C4.

encounters.cc: 6-month history of intensely pruritic skin lesions that began on elbows and spread to knees, lower back, and buttocks

lines: 6-month history of intensely pruritic skin lesions that began on elbows and spread to knees, lower back, and buttocks
The patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and celiac disease returns with a new complaint.
She reports that the lesions began on her elbows and have since spread to her knees, lower back, and buttocks.
She denies any recent travel, new medications, or changes in her detergents or soaps.
Her past medical history is significant for iron-deficiency anemia and recurrent oral ulcers.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO three times daily
She has no joint pain, abdominal pain, or diarrhea.
Physical examination reveals clusters of erythematous papules and vesicles over her extensor surfaces.
Dermatopathology (skin biopsy): Subepidermal vesicles with neutrophilic infiltrates

encounters.cc: Joint pain and fatigue for several months with morning stiffness lasting one hour and occasional painless mouth sores

lines: Joint pain and fatigue for several months with morning stiffness lasting one hour and occasional painless mouth sores
The patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and celiac disease returns for rheumatology follow-up.
She reports morning stiffness lasting about an hour that improves slightly with movement.
She also mentions having occasional painless mouth sores and increased hair loss recently.
She denies fever, cough, or recent infections.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO three times daily
On examination, temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 132/78 mmHg, pulse is 76/min, and respirations are 14/min.
There is mild tenderness of both wrists without swelling or erythema.
Oral examination shows shallow ulcers on the buccal mucosa.
Cardiopulmonary and neurologic examinations are normal.

encounters.cc: 3-month history of intermittent joint pains throughout body, notably worse in hands, with recent painful mouth ulcer

lines: 3-month history of intermittent joint pains throughout body, notably worse in hands, with recent painful mouth ulcer
The patient is a 31-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and celiac disease who returns for follow-up evaluation.
She reports intermittent joint pains throughout her body, but she says they're worse in her hands on most occasions.
Today her fingers are notably sore.
After further questioning, she acknowledges that she had a painful mouth ulcer a few months ago that self-resolved after about a week and a half.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO three times daily
Her father had an episode of deQuervain thyroiditis several years ago.
Laboratory studies show antibodies against the nuclear Smith antigen.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue, shortness of breath, dark urine, and mild yellowing of eyes over the past 3 weeks

lines: Progressive fatigue, shortness of breath, dark urine, and mild yellowing of eyes over the past 3 weeks
The patient with established SLE and celiac disease presents with progressive fatigue and shortness of breath over the past 3 weeks.
She also notes dark urine and mild yellowing of her eyes.
She has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) but is currently not on immunosuppressive therapy.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO three times daily
On examination, she has scleral icterus and mild splenomegaly.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue and mild jaundice with acute worsening requiring hospital admission for transfusion support

lines: Progressive fatigue and mild jaundice with acute worsening requiring hospital admission for transfusion support
Presents with progressive fatigue and mild jaundice over the past month.
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO three times daily
On examination, she has mild scleral icterus but no hepatosplenomegaly
Laboratory studies reveal hemoglobin of 8.2 g/dL, reticulocyte count of 8%, and elevated indirect bilirubin.
Her direct Coombs test is positive, and urinalysis is negative for hemoglobin.
Peripheral smear shows spherocytes without schistocytes.
